title: Service catalogue entries
summary: What every service records in the service catalogue, so that anyone can find who owns it, how critical it is and who to call when it breaks.
scope: Every service, job and library that runs or is published from a company repository.

requirements.title: Every service is in the catalogue
requirements.statement: Every service that runs in a company environment has an entry in the service catalogue before it first takes traffic.
requirements.rationale: During an incident or an audit, a service nobody can find has no owner.
guidance: Follow the process 'Register a service in the service catalogue'.

verification.description: Weekly comparison of the namespaces on the clusters with the catalogue.

requirements.title: Owner team and tier are set
requirements.statement: Each entry names an owner team from the teams list and a tier, and both are kept current.
requirements.rationale: Reviews, alerts and access requests are routed by owner and tier.
guidance: Change the owner in catalog-info.yaml in the same week a service moves to another team.

lookFor: A catalog-info.yaml without spec.owner or without the tier annotation
An owner that is a person instead of a team

requirements.title: On-call contact for production services
requirements.statement: Entries of production services link to the PagerDuty schedule that answers for them.
requirements.rationale: The service desk needs to know who to page without asking around.

verification.description: Report of production services without an on-call link.

requirements.title: Link the documentation
requirements.statement: Entries may link the service's runbook, API description and decision records.
requirements.rationale: One page with every link saves new team members a lot of searching.
